rulings.raw: 2 lbs boneless pork chops ((1 1/4 inch thick, loin chops))
rulings.evidence: Bone-in loin chops carry 15-25% bone and price roughly 30-50% lower per lb, so the generic pork-chops id is a different price class - the same reasoning the estate used on 2026-08-26 to refuse the bone-in/boneless chicken thigh bridge. Registrar should ALIAS to pork-chops if that commodity's captured products are in fact boneless loin chops.
White and yellow cooking onions sell from the same bulk bags at the same price class, unlike red (which the estate rejects on variety pricing); precedent 'small yellow onion' -> onions, board 7 of 7.
celery is a live board id (6 of 7, cheapest 1.88 Hy-Vee) - a reuse; 'stalk' is the cut, not a different food. Only a vocabulary name row is missing.

The line says cranberries with no 'dried', and the method sautes them with the vegetables until soft, which is the fresh berry; fresh-cranberries is a live id (1 of 7 is carriage, not identity). Dried would be a different food at 60 g and 190 cal.
carrots is a live board id at 7 of 7 - a reuse; shredded is a knife cut of the same whole carrot, not a form flip to a bagged product at this quantity.
Plain sandwich bread cubed for a stuffing; `bread` is a live board id (4 of 7, cheapest 1.69 Fareway), so a reuse. Not the dry bouillon-cube foods the FDC shelf offered.
